species.real: Polynesian people once lived on Henderson Island and then left. The flightless crakes stayed, and have hung on alongside the Pacific rats those settlers brought.
species.name: Crakeling

dex.text: A black chick the size of a teacup, with ruby eyes and no interest whatsoever in flying. It runs under the scrub with its beak down, like a very small man late for a very small train.
dex.fact: The Henderson crake is a flightless rail found only on Henderson Island, in the Pitcairn group. Chicks are glossy black with red eyes, and the species has managed to survive alongside introduced Pacific rats.

species.real: Rails have lost the power of flight again and again on remote islands: with no ground predators about, flying is an expensive habit to keep up.
species.name: Hendercrake

dex.text: Sleek, sooty and entirely on the ground, which is exactly where it likes things. It has outlasted the rats, the pigs and a great many plans, and does not mind who knows it.
dex.fact: Henderson Island is a raised coral atoll and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, listed in 1988 for its near-pristine ecosystem. A 2011 attempt to remove the rats that threaten its birds did not succeed, and conservationists have kept working on it since.
